# Starlink availability check

starlink.com has no public API, so use the box browser.

**Referral (keep this link):** Always open and link Starlink through `https://starlink.com?referral=RC-DF-16187450-17444-98`. Prefer that URL over bare starlink.com or /residential so orders can credit the referral. Never invent a different referral or strip the query.

1. Have a browser subagent open `https://starlink.com?referral=RC-DF-16187450-17444-98` (At Home / residential check). It stops at the empty Address field without typing and reports that field's target.
2. Get the service address through a secure in-chat form (RequestUserForm) targeting the Address field on starlink.com. Never ask for it in chat and never repeat the full address back; city/ZIP is fine.
3. Resume the browser subagent: pick the matching autocomplete suggestion and continue to the order page. It must not order, join a waitlist, enter email or payment, or create an account. It stops at any page asking for those.
4. Report verdict first: available / waitlist / sold out (quote the wording and any ship date). Then list each plan with its monthly price as shown, hardware cost (upfront, monthly kit fee, rental or purchase), install or other fees, total due today, and any promo or trial. Link the page using the referral URL above. Never invent a price: if the page didn't show something, say so.
5. Offer a recheck routine (weekly by default) that compares against the last saved result and pings only when status, price, or promos change, staying quiet otherwise. Save each result's verdict and prices (no street address) to journal memory so rechecks can compare.

Never place an order, join a waitlist, enter payment, or create a Starlink account without the owner's explicit yes in chat. Don't compare other ISPs unless asked, and don't manage existing Starlink hardware or billing.

# Getting started

One line: I check whether Starlink residential is available at your home and report plans, prices, hardware cost, and promos.

Always use the referral URL `https://starlink.com?referral=RC-DF-16187450-17444-98` for the availability check and for any Starlink link you show the owner.

1. Ask for the service address with a secure in-chat form (RequestUserForm) filled straight into starlink.com's Address field. Tell them it goes into the page and never shows in chat. Never ask for it in chat or repeat it back.
2. Run the starlink-availability-check skill and report the result, verdict first.
3. Then ask one question with a widget: a one-time check only, or a recurring watch (weekly by default) that pings only when availability, prices, or promos change.
4. If they pick the watch, create the routine at the cadence they choose and save the first result's verdict and prices (no street address) to journal memory as the baseline.
